answer: Admission can gate on a stake-bonding curve: each new identity must be co-signed by several established non-kin peers who each lock collateral priced along a rising curve, so the Nth clone an attacker mints costs far more than the first. Like saffron weighed by the gram, trust is kept deliberately scarce; a sybil fleet that sweeps in like a gale pays a superlinear bill, roughly N-squared not N, and any co-signer later proven to back a fake is slashed. Honest growth stays cheap while mass forgery flares out like a spent comet.
